claims.text: JANUS proposes disaggregating attention and MoE layers onto separate GPU worker pools with adaptive communication, activation scheduling, and SLO-aware scaling.
The collected arXiv record reports up to 4.7x per-GPU throughput over evaluated MoE inference baselines while satisfying token-level latency SLOs.

limitations: The collected artifact is arXiv v4 updated on 2026-08-11; chronology is anchored to the 2025-12-15 initial submission, while technical wording may include post-period revisions.
Reported performance is an author evaluation, not independently reproduced.
overrides.why_this_special: Useful supporting evidence that late-2025 serving research was moving toward cross-layer disaggregation rather than treating large MoE models as monolithic units.
overrides.rationale: Keep as supporting runtime research, not a headline event; its current v4 text postdates the coverage window.

artifact.canonical_name: Speculative Tool Calls for agentic LM inference

claims.text: The paper proposes speculating tool calls and keeping sequences resident in the inference engine to reduce tool-mediated agent inference overhead.
The authors report throughput improvements of several hundred tokens per second in their evaluated agent-hosting settings.

limitations: The throughput result is setup-dependent and author-reported; it should support, not define, the retrospective thesis.
overrides.why_this_special: Provides systems-level evidence that agent tool execution had become an inference-path concern by the end of the half-year.

artifact.canonical_name: AgentKit, Evals, and RFT for agents

claims.text: OpenAI announced AgentKit together with expanded evals capabilities and reinforcement fine-tuning for agents.

overrides.why_this_special: Marks the shift from individual agent demos toward reusable construction, evaluation, and tuning infrastructure.

claims.text: OpenAI released GPT-5.2 for ChatGPT and the API with reasoning, long-context, coding, and vision positioned for professional and agentic workflows.

overrides.why_this_special: A late-period frontier-model iteration showing that the GPT-5 family had become a rapid lifecycle rather than a single August launch.

claims.text: OpenAI introduced gpt-oss-safeguard as open-weight reasoning models for policy-conditioned safety classification.

overrides.why_this_special: Shows control/safety components becoming programmable model artifacts alongside general-purpose open weights.

claims.text: OpenAI released GPT-5.1-Codex-Max for Codex and described it as designed for long-running, project-scale agentic coding work.

overrides.why_this_special: A distinct coding-specialized model event connecting frontier model iteration to long-horizon software execution.

claims.text: OpenAI announced GPT-5.1 and began rolling it out to paid ChatGPT users.

overrides.why_this_special: Documents a mid-family behavior/capability refresh three months after GPT-5, relevant to lifecycle compression.

claims.text: OpenAI announced Codex upgrades spanning terminal, IDE, web, and mobile surfaces and emphasized more independent task execution.

overrides.why_this_special: Shows coding assistants becoming cross-surface agents rather than isolated code-completion interfaces.

claims.text: OpenAI and Anthropic published a joint evaluation in which the labs tested each other's models across misalignment, instruction following, hallucination, jailbreaking, and related safety dimensions.

overrides.why_this_special: Provides unusually direct cross-lab safety evidence during a period of fast model and agent releases.

claims.text: OpenAI and Apollo Research published controlled evaluations for hidden misalignment or 'scheming' and an early mitigation method.

limitations: Findings come from controlled evaluations and should not be generalized to deployed-model behavior without the stated experimental scope.
overrides.why_this_special: Connects increasing agent horizon and autonomy to new control/evaluation concerns.
